name: veh_speed_MON_128
comment: EGAS-L2 MONITOR ego speed, 1/128 km/h (= veh_speed_FUNC_100 * 32/25). All L2 monitor speed compares are cal_u8_kmh * 0x80 (=*128). NOTE: not every '* 0x80' in these monitors is a speed compare - torque/accel values are also scaled *0x40/*0x80.

name: veh_speed_FUNC_100
comment: FUNCTIONAL ego speed (core ctx0), 0.01 km/h. The functional ACC path uses this; the L2 monitors use veh_speed_MON_128 instead.

name: veh_speed_FUNC_100_ctx1
comment: Functional ego speed, core ctx1 twin of veh_speed_FUNC_100 (0.01 km/h).

name: cru_acc_active_flag
comment: Cruise/ACC-active operating flag (= d000abfc, written by the 0x8031 ACC/DCC state block via FUN_801915ce). GATES the #208 cruise-speed monitor: its floor/latch only runs when cruise/ACC is the active longitudinal controller. This is what makes #208 ACC-specific.

name: MON_acc_long_setpoint
comment: Monitor-domain copy of the cruise/ACC longitudinal setpoint (LSB x0x40), built by FUN_800e37de from the GRA/cruise setpoint block (802c4ee8 <- d0008980/84). Bounded by the #213 monitor (800f4abe) inside speed/dwell rails; shared input across the L2 monitor cluster.

name: EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_A
comment: *** THE genuine ACC min-speed monitor (EGAS-L2 cruise/ACC speed-control plausibility, C_VS_MIN_CRU_MON). Gated on cru_acc_active_flag (d000a113). *** Over cal #208 @0x803896ec. Builds MON_cru_permit_flags (d000d7d1) via the persistent permit memory dc87; OPERATIVE FLOOR = 15-SET (0x80389809) / 7-CLEAR (0x8038980e) -> bit7. BEHAVIOUR: SELF-RECOVERING speed-gated PERMIT -- below the floor with dc87=0 the permit is withheld (ECU does not apply the ACC command), and it re-arms/resumes the moment speed>15 (MED17 openpilot user sees re-enable at ~15 = the SET edge). NOT a key-off-on lockout (that is the Simos); #208 feeds NONE of the torque-limp aggregator bytes and the corpus has no NV/Dem store. d00148be is only the monitor-ENGAGED latch. Fix: set both floor cells to 0.

name: EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_B
comment: Continuation/second pass of EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_A over the same cal #208 (Ghidra-split; enters on live registers). Re-derives the 15/7 floor into MON_cru_permit_flags bit7; shares latch d00148be + counters d00148bf/d000d822.

name: MON_cru_speed_engaged_latch
comment: #208 cruise-speed-monitor ENGAGED latch (NOT the fault). Set 800f006c:793 when cru_acc_active_flag(d000a113) AND d000d7f2 (which includes permit-bit7-SET = *permitted*); CLEARED on cruise-off (a113=0) or recovery (d240==8). Monitor-active state, not a stored fault; all volatile RAM. Below the floor the permit is simply withheld (self-recovering, re-arms at speed>15) -- no key-off-on lockout on MED17 (that was the Simos). Exported as EGAS_mon_diag_status bit0x10 (a per-cycle mirror, zero internal readers).

name: EGAS_mon_diag_status
comment: Shared per-monitor diagnostic status bitfield (Dem status projection). bit0x10 (b4) = a per-cycle MIRROR of MON_cru_speed_engaged_latch (via getter 802184f2) = 'cru-speed monitor engaged', NOT a stored fault. Has ZERO internal readers; the ACC/ESP coordinator 801455ae reads only bits 0x40/0x04. NOT a stored fault: the corpus has no NV/Dem write for this bit, and #208's effect is a self-recovering permit withhold (re-arms at speed>15), not a lockout. The key-off-on hard lockout was the Simos, not MED17.

name: MON_cru_permit_floor_flag
comment: L2 monitor PERSISTENT permit memory: 'vehicle has been in the cruise-speed range'. SET when veh_speed_MON_128 > 15 (0x80389809); CLEARED when speed < 7 (0x8038980e); HOLDS between. Written ONLY in the floor block (800f006c:742 / 800f027c:656), reset NOWHERE -> persists across latch cycles + ACC on/off (zeroed only at key-on). Updated only while the monitor is un-latched (arming phase). -> MON_cru_permit_flags bit7; on the next cycle it arms MON_cru_speed_engaged_latch. The 15 = arm-from-scratch, the 7 = re-arm floor (both live).

name: MON_cru_permit_flags
comment: #208 monitor's private cru-permit bitfield (referenced only in 800f006c/027c). bit7 = MON_cru_permit_floor_flag (15/7). The L2 half of the L1/L2 speed-control plausibility; feeds the d00148be latch, not the ACC control path directly.

name: MON_speed_above17_flag
comment: #208 companion band: SET when veh_speed_MON_128 > C_VS_MON_speed17_SET (0x8038980a=17); CLEARED below 17 - C_VS_MON_speed17_bandwidth2(0x80389808=2) = 15. -> d000d7de. SECONDARY arming window (not the operative floor).

name: MON_speed_17band_state
comment: Latched output of MON_speed_above17_flag (17/15). Secondary arming window for other #208 sub-checks; also read by #213 (800f4abe).

name: C_VS_MON_CRU_permit_SET_15
comment: cal #208 +0x11d, u8 km/h = 15. *** THE operative ACC min-speed lever -- the SET/ARM edge. *** EGAS_L2_cru_speed_monitor_A:737 veh_speed_MON_128 > 15*128 -> permit bit7=1 -> the engaged-latch ARMS. The 15/7 floor block runs ONLY while the latch=0 (:728); once armed it holds until ACC-off. The permit memory dc87 is persistent (never reset); with dc87=0 (fresh key-on below 15, or after dropping below 7) the latch never arms and the ACC command is withheld below 15. Set cal=0 -> dc87 arms at any speed>0. Set WITH CLR_7 (7->0, so dc87 never clears) for a re-engage-robust fix. Recompute cal checksum.

name: C_VS_MON_CRU_permit_CLR_7
comment: cal #208 +0x122, u8 km/h = 7. RE-ARM / memory-clear edge -- LIVE. 800f006c:742 `speed < 7*128` clears dc87 (MON_cru_permit_floor_flag), a PERSISTENT hysteretic memory (SET at 15, CLEAR at 7, written only in the floor block, reset nowhere). dc87 holds across latch/ACC cycles, so once =1 you can drop and RE-ENGAGE ACC down to 7; below 7 (un-latched) dc87 clears -> must exceed 15 to re-arm. The floor block runs only while un-latched (arming phase), so this edge is live on every (re-)engagement. Set cal=0 -> dc87 never clears. Set with SET_15.

name: C_VS_MON_speed17_SET
comment: cal #208 +0x11e, u8 km/h = 17. SET edge of the secondary 17/15 band (MON_speed_above17_flag). Clear = 17 - 0x80389808(2) = 15. SECONDARY (arms other sub-checks), not the operative floor. Move with the primary floor for L1/L2 consistency if needed.

name: C_VS_MON_speed17_bandwidth2
comment: cal #208 +0x11c, u8 km/h = 2. Hysteresis BAND WIDTH (subtracted) for the 17-band -> clear edge 15. Relative band, leave stock.

name: EGAS_L2_ACC_longsetpoint_band_213
comment: ACC-relevant (indirect) EGAS-L2 monitor of the ACC/GRA longitudinal setpoint (cal #213 @0x8038a3c8). Bounds MON_acc_long_setpoint (d000d5aa) inside speed/dwell-dependent accel/torque rails (d000d832/d834); debounced sub-faults FEED #208 (d000d829/d82a/d842 -> 800f006c) and the aggregator (d83c/d/e -> FUN_800d9936 -> d344 -> aa23 -> 0x8031 ACC/DCC ctrl). GENUINE speed edges: 0x8038a4ec(=0, moving/standstill) and 0x8038a4ed(=25, sub-check enable). The cells 0x8038a4d7/d8/d9(=16/18/16) and 0x8038a4ee(=12) are torque/accel RAIL coefficients + hysteresis, NOT speed floors..

name: EGAS_L2_cru_lowspeed_crawl_215
comment: ACC-relevant (indirect) EGAS-L2 cruise/ACC low-speed CRAWL monitor (cal #215 @0x8038a568). Fault severity d000d857 -> cruise fault-reaction manager 800dca9c (can force fault/off via d000d3fc) + aggregator 800d9936. Two-stage state machine d000d858/d859 (cases 0-3). Its crawl trip runs ONLY in the failsafe branch (when internal signal 0x3fc is STALE - runs at startup/on-message-loss, NOT proven dead). Speed cells 0x8038a5c9/ca(=6)/cd(=5) are crawl ARMING windows, 0x8038a5c6(=20) an upper counter-reset bound, 0x8038a5cb(=0) DISABLES a d859 transition. Not an ACC engage floor..

name: EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator
comment: THE EGAS-Level-2 monitor DTC/fault aggregator. AND-masks ~8-15 monitor result bytes (from 800f25e2/800f40bc/800f5d68/800f5982/800f4abe/...) with cal enables into fault dwords d000d32c/d334/d338, computes overall verdict d000d344 (0-3 severity) -> d000aa23 (read by the 0x8031 ACC/DCC controller) = the EGAS-3 torque-limitation/limp reaction. Terminal sink for all L2 monitors.

name: EGAS_L2_fault_verdict
comment: Overall EGAS-L2 fault verdict/severity (0-3) from EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. Copied to EGAS_L2_reaction_level (d000aa23) via FUN_802c51c2; drives the engine torque-limitation/limp reaction.

name: EGAS_L2_reaction_level
comment: = EGAS_L2_fault_verdict (d000d344). Read by the 0x8031 ACC/DCC controller functions (80312f70/803147dc/80315a54, mirrored to d000abed) - the ACC-facing effect of a confirmed L2 monitor fault (torque limp).

name: EGAS_L2_torque_monitor_209_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - general engine-torque EGAS-L2 plausibility (Momentenueberwachung), cal #209 @0x80389868. Compares model vs permitted torque, debounces faults into d000deea/deeb -> packed df0a-0d -> EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. Speed cells 0x8038a205/206/207 (8/5/0) are torque-check low-speed windows; 0x8038a202-204 (255/255/254) DISABLE their speed gates. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_monitor_214_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - general EGAS-L2 torque-vs-speed plausibility, cal #214 @0x8038a514. 0x8038a551(=10) is a low-speed SUPPRESSION term for a torque check, not an ACC floor. Latches a held verdict d000d846 -> EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_plaus_seq_173_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 sequential torque-plausibility, cal #173 @0x80385c4c. Its 0x8038679b(=15) is the LOWER BOUND of a torque-window [15,105] arming a corridor check on MON_acc_long_setpoint - a numerical coincidence, NOT the C_VS_MIN_CRU_MON floor. All state volatile, no non-volatile latch, no ACC var referenced. Do NOT edit for openpilot.

name: EGAS_L2_channel_plaus_211_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 redundant channel/pedal plausibility voting, cal #211 @0x8038a25a. 0x8038a3a4(=255) is a de-facto DISABLED 255 km/h over-speed ceiling; other speed uses are axis/threshold selects. Packs df2d/2e/2f -> EGAS_L2_fault_aggregator. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_coordinator_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 permitted-vs-actual longitudinal torque check. Enabled only in a 25-130 km/h driving window (the opposite of a low-speed floor). Sets monitor result d000e036. No ACC coupling.

name: EGAS_L2_accel_torque_model_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 longitudinal accel/torque MODEL. Vehicle speed is a MAP AXIS input, not a floor. Contains the MONITOR twin of the +/-500000 decel rail (the monitor's own authority, not the functional one). Outputs d000d5xx monitor group.

name: EGAS_L2_roadload_model_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 road-load/driving-resistance model: v^2 aero drag + v rolling + accel terms -> resistance shadows d000dfe2/e8 (feeds EGAS_L2_torque_coordinator 800fb796). Speed used as physical model axis, not a threshold.

name: EGAS_L2_step_dtc_manager_193_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 operating-step sequencer + DTC manager, cal #193 @0x80387f5c. 0x80387fbc(=6) gates only the internal step-active flag d000d6f7 in coast-state (SUPPRESSES the sequencer at low speed). No ACC var referenced.

name: EGAS_L2_torque_plaus_148_NOTACC
comment: NOT an ACC monitor - EGAS-L2 monitor-domain torque plausibility, cal #148 @0x8038436a. PROVABLY produces no low-speed fault: double-gated (subsystem-state d3cd in {3,8} + operating-point>=80, then hysteresis d000d867 SET>12 / CLEAR<5 via 0x80384761=5 low-edge + 0x80384760=7 band-width) -> self-disables below ~12 km/h. Outputs feed only telemetry+getter. No ACC coupling.

name: ACC_master_state_machine
comment: ACC/GRA master state machine. Transition table @0x80044772 (134 entries): a3c1 (ACC_master_mode, out_idx 0x1b) = a DIRECT COPY of cond[0x1c] = the 2-bit commanded mode. NO engine-side speed floor gates engagement; it relays the commanded ACC mode (openpilot via ACC_01).

name: statemachine_unpack_cond_vector
comment: Unpacks the 10-byte packed ACC condition vector into 50 condition slots (1-3 bits each). cond[0x1c]=byte5[5:6]=the 2-bit ACC mode -> ACC_master_mode.

name: statemachine_confirm_transition
comment: Transition-confirm layer over ACC_cond_vec_current (d0009b63) vs _new (d0009b70) via descriptor 0x8003f374. Event-driven; no speed compare.

name: statemachine_load_cond_vec_coding
comment: Loads the ACC engage-condition vector from the CODING data store, not from an event mailbox. FUN_8008ebbc(&UNK_d0009b48,&d000b9ad,0xe,0,0x34) reads a 52-byte record from store class 0xe (a coding/config store: sibling reads use records 0x14/0x16/0x1b/0x33 with sizes 1-10 and each has a flash fallback). The other branch copies the flash coding default DAT_803def94 into ACC_cond_vec_current/_new. So a3c1 (ACC master mode) is CODING-determined, not event-driven; there is no runtime condition-event producer to find. FUN_8008ebbc posts a request into the 8-slot service ring at d0006a10 and spins on FUN_8008f464 until serviced -- it is a synchronous store read, not an async mailbox.

name: ACC_cond_vec_current
comment: Current packed ACC engage-condition vector (10 bytes). byte5[5:6] = commanded ACC mode -> ACC_master_mode.

name: ACC_cond_vec_new
comment: Candidate/new packed ACC engage-condition vector; confirmed into ACC_cond_vec_current.

name: ACC_master_mode
comment: ACC/GRA master mode: 0=inactive,1=GRA,2=ACC,3=ACC-extended = direct copy of engage condition slot 0x1c. Feeds d000a454 via FUN_802c806e. No engine-side speed floor gates this.

name: ACC_status_rx
comment: RX-side ACC status index, unpacked by FUN_800b1136 from ACC_01 (0x109) bit 60 len 3 = ACC_Status_ACC. PROVEN from the COM signal-descriptor table (record @0x80038ad8, desc 0x0000033c), not inferred; corroborated by on-car CAN where openpilot's commanded status maps 1:1 through tbl[] to TSK_04. A second descriptor @0x80038a60 binds the same byte from bit 57 len 3 (platform variant). -> a368 via FUN_800b0e94.

name: ACC_state_a368
comment: ACC state enum (0=off 1=engaged 2=engaged+override 3=fault). Sole writer FUN_800b0e94: a368 = tbl[ACC_status_rx], tbl_A@0x8004579a=[0,0,2,1,1,0,2,3] (selectors 0x55/0x73), tbl_B@0x800457a2=[0,0,0,1,2,0,0,3] (selectors 0x2a/0x56); selector 0x29 uses d000a5a4 directly. Copied to ab01 by FUN_801455ae.

name: TSK04_status_ab01
comment: Source shadow for TSK_04 (0x10E) TSK_Status_GRA_ACC_02 (62|2). = ACC_state_a368, forced to 3 when the present-gate word is nonzero, and forced to 0 by the FUN_801455ae suppressor (ab01 in {1,2} AND d0000121 bit5, zero debounce -- cal #251 +0xc/+0xe are both 0). Case 0 rails the request outputs: d0005f20 = d0005d00 = -500000.

name: GE_Waehlhebel_rx
comment: Gear SELECTOR LEVER position, from Getriebe_03 (0x102) bit 44 len 4 = GE_Waehlhebel. PROVEN: COM descriptor record @0x80039c08 (desc 0x42c) sits in the Getriebe_03 PDU group @0x80039be0 (75% DBC geometry match), and the on-car log shows the P->R->N->D sequence 5->6->7->8 at drive start and the reverse at drive end. NOT a cruise state -- an earlier label (cru_state_rx) was wrong. Read only by FUN_80087a70.

name: gear_sel_state
comment: Mapped gear-selector state = tbl[GE_Waehlhebel_rx] (FUN_80087a70, sole writer). tbl@0x800453b4 = identity[0..14] when (d0008c80 & 0x610)==0 && (d0008c80 & 0x1000)==0, else tbl@0x80045395 = [0,0,0,0,0,8,7,6,5,12,17,0,0,14,14]. States {6,8} = selector in R or D (FUN_80087a70 computes that same test at its tail). Shadowed to d0009f76 for the L2 monitor.

name: gear_sel_state_MON
comment: L2-monitor shadow copy of gear_sel_state (802c4942:155 / 802c4ee8:28). Classified by FUN_8010295e(cal#208+0x49,+0x36,.) whose LUT @0x80389735 is an IDENTITY map over 0..17, so monitor state == gear_sel_state. Feeds d7ed = debounce(state==6) and d7f1 = debounce(state==8) -- i.e. selector in R / in D.

name: MON_cru_active_permit
comment: #208 suppression term holding d7f9 low during normal engaged driving. With cfg word cal#208+0x148 = 0x1bf3 (@0x80389834) collapsing terms 1-2 to always-true: dc8b = cru_acc_active_flag(a113) && d000d240<=8 && d000a0a9 && (gear_sel_state == 6 || == 8), i.e. GEAR SELECTOR IN R OR D. Copied to d7f6 one cycle later. NOTE: the selector was constant at D across the whole on-car log, so this term cannot explain the ~15 km/h ACC drop.

name: MON_cru_floor_fault
comment: #208's output into the EGAS-L2 fault aggregator (written 800f006c:728, read 800d9936:71). Set when d240==8 AND the d00148bf counter < cal#208+0xec AND MON_cru_permit_flags bit7 is CLEAR (below the 15 km/h floor / unarmed) AND d7f6==0. This is the path by which the min-speed monitor reaches the ACC command: d7f9 -> aggregator -> EGAS_L2_fault_verdict -> EGAS_L2_reaction_level -> the 0x8031 ACC/DCC controller.

name: ACC_Sollbeschleunigung_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 24 len 11 = ACC_Sollbeschleunigung -- the COMMANDED ACCEL entry point into the ECU. PROVEN from the COM signal-descriptor table: record @0x80038ba0 (desc 0x0003_0b18) inside the contiguous ACC_01 RX group @0x80038ad8..0x80038bc8 (stride 0x28, descending bit order). Written by the RX unpacker FUN_800b1136 and by the timeout-substitution setter FUN_8008b17c. -> d000830a.

name: ACC_zul_Regelabw_unten_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 16 len 6 = ACC_zul_Regelabw_unten. COM descriptor record @0x80038bc8, ACC_01 RX group. -> d000830c via FUN_800b1136.

name: ACC_zul_Regelabw_oben_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 35 len 5 = ACC_zul_Regelabw_oben. COM descriptor record @0x80038b78, ACC_01 RX group. -> d000830e via FUN_800b1136.

name: ACC_neg_Sollbeschl_Grad_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 40 len 8 = ACC_neg_Sollbeschl_Grad (negative jerk limit). COM descriptor record @0x80038b50. -> d0008310 via FUN_800b1136, with a '< 4 -> use default' floor.

name: ACC_pos_Sollbeschl_Grad_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 48 len 8 = ACC_pos_Sollbeschl_Grad (positive jerk limit). COM descriptor record @0x80038b28. -> d0008312 via FUN_800b1136, with a '< 4 -> use default' floor.

name: ACC_Dynamik_rx
comment: ACC_01 (0x109) bit 58 len 2 = ACC_Dynamik. COM descriptor record @0x80038b00, ACC_01 RX group. Read by FUN_800b0e94.

name: ACC_cmd_accel
comment: The commanded accel inside the ECU = ACC_Sollbeschleunigung after RX unpack (FUN_800b1136 selector 0x55). Validity is gated there: d00001af bit6 SET iff ACC_status_rx in {3,4}, else d0000159 bit2 (substitute). Sole reader FUN_80140922, which copies it UNCLAMPED to d00082ae.

name: TSK_cmd_accel_shadow
comment: Commanded accel handed to the TSK path: FUN_80140922 (gated d000a454==2) copies d000830a here with NO clamp. Read by FUN_801418ea, which clamps it into a speed-indexed envelope -> d00082c4.

name: TSK_accel_clamped
comment: Commanded accel after the FUN_801418ea envelope clamp: d00082c4 = max(limit_B, min(limit_A, d00082ae)) where BOTH limits are speed-indexed curve lookups over cal #247 (0x803b4834). MEASURED FLAT on this image: lower -3.0 m/s^2, upper +2.0 m/s^2 at every speed -- i.e. no speed-dependent accel limiting. -> d00082b6 (TSK_04) and d00082c0 (TSK_02).

name: TSK_ax_Getriebe_tx
comment: TSK_04 (0x10E) bit 18 len 9 = TSK_ax_Getriebe. COM descriptor record @0x80039258, inside the contiguous TSK_04 group @0x80039190+k*0x28. Sole writer FUN_8014469a: substituted with cal 0x803b508a (=0, packs to wire raw 84 = +0.000 m/s^2) whenever the bVar11 gate is false. Matches the on-car neutral exactly.

name: TSK_zul_Regelabw_tx
comment: TSK_04 (0x10E) bit 12 len 6 = TSK_zul_Regelabw. COM descriptor record @0x80039280. Written by FUN_80140922 from d000830c via func_0xc0000926(x,1000,10000).

name: TSK_Wunsch_Uebersetz_tx
comment: TSK_04 (0x10E) bit 27 len 10 = TSK_Wunsch_Uebersetz (gear-ratio request). COM descriptor record @0x80039230, TSK_04 group.

name: TSK_Verzoeg_Anf_tx
comment: TSK_02 (0x10C) bit 56 len 8 = TSK_Verzoeg_Anf -- the DECEL REQUEST the engine sends to ESP. COM descriptor record @0x800392f8 (TSK_02 group with TSK_Status 16|2 and TSK_Radbremsmom 40|12). Written by FUN_801405d4: 'uVar8 = 0; if (bVar1) uVar8 = d00082c0;' -- a HARD ZERO when the gate is false, which is the measured wire raw 166 = 0.000 m/s^2. bVar1 = (a362 in {1,5}) chain, i.e. ACC actively regulating.

name: TSK_Radbremsmom_tx
comment: TSK_02 (0x10C) bit 40 len 12 = TSK_Radbremsmom (wheel-brake torque request). COM descriptor record @0x80039320, TSK_02 group.

name: TSK_amax_moeglich_tx
comment: TSK_01 (0x10A) bit 48 len 9 = TSK_amax_moeglich. COM descriptor record @0x80039d48. Stays LIVE below the ACC floor on-car (99 distinct values, 0.000..6.072 m/s^2, tracking speed) -- the engine keeps publishing capability while withholding the request.

name: ACC_lowspeed_flag_15kmh
comment: *** THE 15 km/h CONDITION. *** Populated from INTERNAL message 0x466 (handle @0x800284b6, the only copy in the image; read via the COM receive in FUN_800a5db0). Drives d000015f bit 7 (that bit has no other writer) -> d00000e0 bit 7 -> d0004985 -> debounce(cal 0x8010384c+0x5e) -> d000f82a bit 7 -> TSK_01 (0x10A) FRAME BIT 23, which on-car is SET 0..15.28 km/h, CLEAR above, transitions at 15.08/14.90/15.38/14.88 km/h and LEADS the ACC drop by one 20 ms frame. PRODUCER NOT IN THE DISASSEMBLY: its only writers are the circular per-context shadow pair with d000ab6a; no block copy covers it; not a COM descriptor target; a 649-function guarded gap-walk added no writer. DOUBLE-CONFIRMED NEGATIVE: a linear constant-propagation scan of the EFFECTIVE ADDRESS of every memory access in all 5918 functions (core/ghidra/FindEffectiveAddr.java, which closes FindRefsTo's blind spot for base+displacement stores that leave no reference on the target byte) also finds ONLY the three circular shadow writers. Caveat: that scan seeds a0/a1/a8/a9 from ecu.conf, so a producer whose base register comes from a runtime table resolves as INDEXED rather than as a hit -- the negative is 'no resolvable-EA writer', not an absolute one. ADDRESSING FORM (this is why no literal exists): a6c7 is reached as `lea aX,[a0]-0x1d59` with a0 = 0xd000c420 (the global data base from ecu.conf BASEREGS); 0xd000c420-0x1d59 = 0xd000a6c7. Known encoding: bytes d9 <(base<<4)|dest> 27 ae. A raw-image scan for ANY 32-bit instruction carrying displacement bytes 27 ae returns 9 hits: the 6 known [a0] sites, one FALSE POSITIVE at 0x80101866 (base a15=0xd0010000 -> targets d000e2a7, not a6c7), and 2 in the 0x8002xxxx constant-pool region that are data, not code. So NO undisassembled code accesses a6c7 via this form -- a third independent method agreeing with the reference-model and effective-address scans. RESIDUAL GAP: a store through a base pointing NEAR a6c7 with a non-zero store offset (e.g. lea to a6a0 then st.b [aX]0x27) would carry a DIFFERENT displacement and evade this byte scan in undisassembled code; FindEffectiveAddr covers that case but only for disassembled functions. FIFTH AND SIXTH ELIMINATIONS: (5) a0 is formed exactly ONCE in the whole image (0x800829d6 = 0xd000c420, per analysis/basereg.log) so the [a0]-relative addressing assumption behind every scan is sound -- there is no second context with a different a0. RESOLVED: segment 0xC is the CPU-LOCAL PROGRAM SCRATCHPAD (PMI), not LMU. Evidence from the image itself, not a datasheet: the MPU region table at 0x8003fa60 splits segment 0xC into c0000000-c000013f / c0000140-c000019f / c00001a0-c000039f as data (totalling exactly 0x3a0) and c00003a0-c0007fff as code -- and the code copy lands at exactly 0xc00003a0, that boundary. On TriCore, segment 12 is architecturally the PMI local code memory. This is also why tricore tc176x.pspec (modelling TC1762/TC1766) declares nothing there. Distinct from the boot-ROM targets: those are 0xAFFFF100/0xAFFFF110 (NOT 0xafff0100/0110 as first recorded), 4 calli sites in FUN_80016c08/FUN_80017076. 0xAFFF0000-0xAFFFFFFF is the Infineon on-chip BOOT ROM (mask ROM), so they are PERMANENTLY unrecoverable from any flash dump -- an exhaustive scan for a copy record with a segment-0xA destination returns 0 matches, as does one for SPRAM 0xd4000000. Scale of the segment-0xC recovery: 27 branch targets give 27 clean function prologues, behind 2140 call sites in 569 distinct flash functions (9.6% of the corpus).

name: COM_msg_common_callback
comment: The single callback value at +0x08 of every record in the CAN message table 0x800312d0 (all 48 records). Its uniformity is what makes '+0x08 == 0x80029652' a reliable structural check when validating the table extent on another image.

name: COM_desc_callback_alt
comment: Alternate signal-descriptor conversion callback at descriptor +0x0c, used by TSK_01's 24-bit status record 0x80039460 instead of the common 0x800286c6. Keying a descriptor scan on a single callback value silently drops records that use this one -- the reason COM_DESC_CB alone under-scans the table.

name: boot_copy_table_data
comment: Boot .data initialiser table, 12-byte records in (src, dst, len) order -- note the OPPOSITE field order to 0x800402ec; a 0xffffffff record terminates. Decoded: 0x800045c0 -> 0xc0001400 len 0x80; 0x80004640 -> 0xc0001500 len 0x248; 0x80004888 -> 0xd0000ac8 len 0x9408; 0x8000dc90 -> 0xd0009ed0 len 0x270; 0x8000df00 -> 0xd000a140 len 0x968. The third entry is the 39 KB LDRAM data image and it is what explains FUN_d00098fa: 0x80004888 + (0xd00098fa - 0xd0000ac8) = 0x8000d6ba, so those bytes are INITIALISED DATA copied into RAM, not resident code -- seven functions build small-data-area pointers into that window via a0 and WRITE to it. Treat FUN_d00098fa as an artefact to reclassify, not code to decode. Also note the 0xc0001400/0xc0001500 destinations land INSIDE the 0x800402ec code alias, so segment 0xC holds code and initialised data together and a single flat alias over it is approximate for those two sub-ranges.

name: boot_copy_table_load
comment: Boot load-image copy table, 12-byte records (dst, src, len). Several records have len=0 and are no-ops (rec0/rec3/rec7); src=0xffffffff or a repeated byte pattern marks a FILL. Live records: 0xd000bfd8 <- 0x80024f90 len 0xdb0 (.data); 0xd000cd88 <- 0x80025d40 len 0x1558 (.data); 0xc00003a0 <- 0x80020098 len 0x12d0 (TriCore code run from segment 0xC); 0xf0060000 <- 0x800222e8 len 0x2ca8; 0xf0050000 <- 0x80021368 len 0xf80; fills 0xc0001670 len 0x6990, 0xf0062ca8 len 0x1358, 0xf0050f80 len 0x1080. Sources are contiguous 0x80020098..0x80027298. *** 0xF0050000 and 0xF0060000 are the TC1797 PCP2 (Peripheral Control Processor) memories: the FILLs terminate at exactly 0xf0052000 (8 KB) and 0xf0064000 (16 KB), the PCP2 memory sizes. 0xF0060000 = CMEM (code), so 0x800222e8 len 0x2ca8 (11432 bytes) is PCP MICROCODE -- a SECOND PROCESSOR's firmware, in a different instruction set that Ghidra's TriCore model can never decode. 0xF0050000 = PRAM (0xf80). This is a real, permanently bounded slice of the 'unaccounted' byte gap. (CORRECTION: an earlier revision of this row gave the table start as 0x800402ec -- that is record 4, mid-table -- and had the CMEM/PRAM roles reversed.)

name: ram_vtable_main
comment: The image's real RAM function-pointer table: 155 entries, 132 distinct targets, all in 0xd0000ac8-0xd000aaa8. It is exactly copy-record 4 of table 0x8000e868 (src 0x8000dc90, len 0x270 = 156 words), i.e. a dedicated vtable materialised at boot. Companions: 0xd000a3fc (5), 0xd000a414 (4), 0xd000a458 (4), 0xd000aa08 (8). Because the flash boot sector 0x80000000..0x80004000 is entirely zero, the crt0 that CONSUMES these tables is absent from the dump -- which is why no code references the copy tables and why emulating the copy can never work. Applying the tables statically is exact and needs no emulator.

name: boot_rom_entry_points
comment: 0xAFFFF100 / 0xAFFFF110, called via 4 calli sites in FUN_80016c08 and FUN_80017076. Infineon on-chip BOOT ROM (mask ROM) -- not present in any flash dump and not copied there by any table in the image. PERMANENTLY out of scope for static recovery; record as a hard boundary, not an open lead.

name: Kennlinie_s16
comment: Part of the segment-0xC (PSPR) library, recovered this session by mapping the boot copy table -- before that every call site here was an unmapped address and the ACC/TSK decompiles were full of holes. Layout established by reading the code, not assumed. 1-D characteristic-curve (Kennlinie) interpolation, SIGNED 16-bit: FUN(short *tbl, int x). Layout tbl[0]=n, tbl[1..n]=X breakpoints, tbl[n+1..2n]=Y values; binary search over X then linear interpolate. 286 call sites. THIS MATTERS FOR SEARCHING: a threshold in this ECU is often a curve BREAKPOINT, not a scalar compare, so scanning cal reads for a constant cannot find it -- decode the curves instead. Verified against table 0x803dcd64 (n=5, X=200/500/1000/1500/2000 = 2..20 km/h).

Layout established by reading the code, not assumed. 1-D Kennlinie, UNSIGNED 16-bit: FUN(ushort *tbl, int x). Same layout as Kennlinie_s16 (tbl[0]=n, X at [1..n], Y at [n+1..2n]). 270 call sites.

Same layout as Kennlinie_s16 but u8 elements (tbl[0]=n, X at [1..n], Y at [n+1..2n]). 240 call sites.

name: Kennfeld_s16
comment: Part of the segment-0xC (PSPR) library, recovered this session by mapping the boot copy table -- before that every call site here was an unmapped address and the ACC/TSK decompiles were full of holes. Layout established by reading the code, not assumed. 2-D characteristic-map (Kennfeld) interpolation, SIGNED 16-bit: FUN(short *tbl, int x, int y). Layout tbl[0]=nx, tbl[1]=ny, X breakpoints at [2..nx+1], Y breakpoints at [nx+2..nx+ny+1], then nx*ny Z values. Derived from the code: psVar17 = tbl+1+nx walks the Y axis and the first X compare is tbl[2]. 204 call sites.

comment: Part of the segment-0xC (PSPR) library, recovered this session by mapping the boot copy table -- before that every call site here was an unmapped address and the ACC/TSK decompiles were full of holes. Layout established by reading the code, not assumed. 2-D Kennfeld, UNSIGNED 8-bit: FUN(byte *tbl, int x, int y). Same [nx, ny, X.., Y.., Z..] layout as Kennfeld_s16 (tbl[0]=nx, tbl[1]=ny, axes from tbl+2). 73 call sites.

name: satdiv_32_16
comment: Part of the segment-0xC (PSPR) library, recovered this session by mapping the boot copy table -- before that every call site here was an unmapped address and the ACC/TSK decompiles were full of holes. Layout established by reading the code, not assumed. Saturating signed 32/32 -> int16 restoring divide (shift-subtract loop). 224 call sites; heavily used by the ACC accel/decel arithmetic, e.g. FUN_802feaa0 resolves to (x*65536 + 120)/240 saturated once this is decodable. [I] -- read from the disassembly, not proven against a reference implementation.

name: acc_lowspeed_curve_zeroed
comment: 1-D Kennlinie (see 0xc0000638) on the ACC path: n=5, X = 200/500/1000/1500/2000 = 2.00/5.00/10.00/15.00/20.00 km/h -- exactly the low-speed band -- and Y = 0/0/0/0/0. Reached from the 0x80146xxx family via PTR_DAT_801040f4+0x318. NOT DEMONSTRATED TO BE THE 15 km/h FLOOR, and recorded here so the lead is not re-chased: the alternative branch (scalar +0x32e) is ALSO 0, so both arms of the if/else yield zero and the term is inert; the value is SUBTRACTED as an offset rather than used as a limit; and 7 of the 29 ACC-reachable curves are all-zero, so a zeroed curve is unremarkable in this calibration. Consistent with a low-speed feature present but calibrated inert (cf. the B8 single-radar 30 km/h floor), which is a hypothesis, not a finding.

name: acc_lowspeed_map_neutral
comment: 2-D Kennfeld (see 0xc00004ca) used by the same 0x80146xxx family: nx=5, ny=6, X = 500..2500 (5..25 km/h), Y = 400..2400, and Z uniformly 10000. A constant map applies no shaping, so like 0x803dcd64 it is low-speed-indexed but neutral. Also NOT shown to be the floor.
